METHOD: Filtered V1's standardized SIPA output to series_identifier=SIPA-T2-LEVEL-ORIGINAL (GOV-010: A.1 and T.2.1 are the same series; T.2 is V1's designated canonical level representation). For each of the two endpoint months (first and last available in the T.2 table), computed each named modality's share as value / (sum of the six named modalities: ASALARIADO_PRIVADO, ASALARIADO_PUBLICO, AUTONOMO, CASAS_PARTICULARES, MONOTRIBUTO, MONOTRIBUTO_SOCIAL). This analytical denominator is a LAB-A construct for share computation only -- it is NOT asserted to be, or to validate, SIPA's own published TOTAL row (GOV-005: TOTAL must not be recomputed by summing modalities). Computed percentage-point change in each modality's share between 2012-01 and 2026-05.
METRIC: Percentage-point change in modality composition share of registered employment, 2012-01 vs 2026-05 (LAB-HYP-0001's pre-registered metric)
RESULT: Shares (2012-01 -> 2026-05, percentage points): ASALARIADO_PRIVADO 55.86% -> 47.89% (-7.97pp); ASALARIADO_PUBLICO 23.27% -> 26.50% (+3.23pp); MONOTRIBUTO 12.03% -> 17.24% (+5.21pp); AUTONOMO 3.75% -> 3.04% (-0.71pp); CASAS_PARTICULARES 3.56% -> 3.51% (-0.05pp); MONOTRIBUTO_SOCIAL 1.53% -> 1.82% (+0.29pp). Three modalities (ASALARIADO_PRIVADO, ASALARIADO_PUBLICO, MONOTRIBUTO) exceed the pre-registered 2 percentage-point threshold; this matches LAB-HYP-0001's EXPECTED_OBSERVATION, not its FAILURE_CONDITION.
LIMITATIONS: Single Evidence Root (SIPA only); cannot be CONVERGENT regardless of result strength (Root Counting Rule requires >=2 INDEPENDENT roots)
T.2 table window (2012-01 onward) is narrower than A.1's full window (2009-01 onward); the 2009-2011 sub-period is not covered by this comparison
ASALARIADO_PUBLICO carries a mandatory extrapolation caveat under GOV-005 (constructed from prior-month percent variation, not a direct recount)

The six-modality sum used as an analytical denominator numerically coincided with SIPA's own published TOTAL row in the two months checked; this is reported as an observation, not asserted as a general validated equivalence, and is not used as evidence toward resolving GOV-005's TOTAL/PUBLICO disposition
Endpoint (two-month) comparison only; does not characterize the full monthly trajectory or rule out non-monotonic movement between 2012 and 2026

METHOD: Filtered V1's standardized CGI output to INDEC's own published national totals (occupational_category=TOTAL, activity_sector=TOTAL_GENERAL for JOB and HOUR; occupational_category=ASALARIADO, activity_sector=TOTAL_GENERAL for WAGE_BILL -- the only occupational_category WAGE_BILL has). Computed year-over-year (same quarter, prior year) percentage growth for each of the 3 series across all 37 quarters where a prior-year quarter exists (2017-Q1 through 2026-Q1). Computed the pairwise absolute difference in YoY growth rate between each pair of series per quarter. All values are NOMINAL (current Argentine pesos); no IPC deflation was applied (IPC is BLOCKED_BY_IPC, not admitted).
METRIC: Pairwise divergence (percentage points) in year-over-year growth rates between JOB, HOUR, and WAGE_BILL (LAB-HYP-0002's pre-registered metric)
RESULT: All three pairwise divergences exceed the pre-registered 1 percentage-point threshold in multiple quarters, far surpassing LAB-HYP-0002's EXPECTED_OBSERVATION. Two distinct patterns: (1) JOB vs HOUR diverge sharply during 2020-2021: 2020-Q2 JOB -16.94% YoY vs HOUR -36.23% YoY (19.29pp gap); 2021-Q2 JOB +17.58% vs HOUR +54.32% (36.75pp gap, the largest JOB-HOUR divergence in the series) -- consistent with intensive-margin (hours-per-job) adjustment around the COVID-19 period. (2) Nominal WAGE_BILL growth diverges massively from JOB/HOUR growth from 2022 onward (e.g. 2024-Q2: JOB +0.73%, HOUR -1.40%, WAGE_BILL +234.30% YoY; a 233-235pp gap) -- this is a large nominal-currency divergence; its real-terms interpretation (including whether it reflects inflation) is deferred pending IPC admission and is not asserted here.
LIMITATIONS: Single Evidence Root (CGI only); JOB, HOUR, and WAGE_BILL are three measures of the same national-accounts product, not independent sources -- cannot be CONVERGENT

WAGE_BILL's nominal divergence from JOB/HOUR is large; its real-terms interpretation is deferred pending IPC admission and is NOT asserted here as a real-wage-bill or purchasing-power finding; no real-value claim is made (BLOCKED_BY_IPC)

2020-2021 is treated as a potentially special period (COVID-19 collection/economic disruption); the JOB-vs-HOUR divergence during this window may reflect measurement or economic conditions specific to that period, not a stable structural relationship

METHOD: DuckDB (read-only, in-process) aggregation of V1's standardized MLER panel for the 120-month SIPA/MLER overlap window (2012-01 to 2021-12): (a) weighted PERSON-adjacent estimate per month = SUM(sample_weight) over one row per (reference_month, worker_id); (b) weighted EMPLOYMENT_RELATIONSHIP-adjacent estimate per month = SUM(sample_weight) over all rows (each row is one worker x relationship_sequence x month). Compared both series against SIPA's SIPA-T2-LEVEL-ORIGINAL ASALARIADO_PRIVADO series (LAB-ROOT-0001) for the same months. No individual MLER record was read or extracted; only the two resulting 120-point monthly aggregate series were retained.
METRIC: Percent difference between MLER-derived and SIPA-derived counts of PERSON-adjacent and EMPLOYMENT_RELATIONSHIP-adjacent fields, within the 2012-01/2021-12 overlap (LAB-HYP-0007's pre-registered metric)
RESULT: (a) PERSON-adjacent: MLER's weighted worker count tracks SIPA's ASALARIADO_PRIVADO level closely across all 120 months -- average absolute difference 0.54%, ranging 0.02% (2013-10) to 0.98% (2021-12). (b) EMPLOYMENT_RELATIONSHIP-adjacent: MLER's weighted relationship count is consistently higher than SIPA's person count, and the gap grows over the period: +3.38% (2012-01) to +5.07% (2021-12), averaging +4.27%. Interpretation: (b) is a clear, measurable, and widening divergence, matching LAB-HYP-0007's EXPECTED_OBSERVATION, and is substantively interpretable as a rising rate of multiple simultaneous job-holding among the same underlying population. (a) is a close but non-zero agreement whose relationship to LAB-HYP-0007's FAILURE_CONDITION ('agree to within stated tolerance') is ambiguous, because no numeric tolerance was pre-specified; this ambiguity is reported honestly rather than resolved by post-hoc threshold selection.
LIMITATIONS: MLER is DOWNSTREAM_PROXY of SIPA (LAB-ROOT-0003 relative to LAB-ROOT-0001; V1 P1 audit C5B: MLER is sampled from the same SIPA/AFIP declaration stream SIPA itself publishes from). The close agreement in (a) is therefore expected by construction and is NOT independent corroboration of the registered-employment count -- CONVERGENT does not apply regardless of numeric closeness (Root Counting Rule: only INDEPENDENT roots count, and this pair is not independent)

LAB-HYP-0007's FAILURE_CONDITION did not pre-specify a numeric tolerance band, making result (a) ambiguous relative to 'agreement within tolerance' versus 'measurable divergence' -- flagged as a hypothesis-design gap for any future LAB-GOV/LAB-A2 refinement, not resolved here
GOV-006 applies throughout: EMPLOYER and JOB are UNREALIZED on the MLER artifact; only PERSON and EMPLOYMENT_RELATIONSHIP (relationship_sequence) were used, never JOB or EMPLOYER
MLER's edition ends 2021-12; this evidence says nothing about 2022-2026 and must not be extrapolated to describe the current labour market
sample_weight-based estimates carry sampling variance not quantified here (no confidence interval computed)
REPRODUCIBILITY: Recomputable via DuckDB read_csv_auto against data/standardized/oede_mler_2021/mler_panel.csv.gz (SHA-256 above) and data/standardized/sipa_trabajo_registrado/sipa_registered_work_monthly.csv (SHA-256 above). The two 120-point monthly aggregate series (not individual records) are archived at reports/lab_a/mler-sipa-overlap-monthly-aggregates.json. Exact SQL and method detailed in reports/lab_a/LAB-A-method.md. Query runtime: ~21 seconds total on this machine (two passes over the 559 MB compressed panel).

METHOD: V1's CGI standardized file (read-only) filtered to occupational_category=ASALARIADO/activity_sector=TOTAL_GENERAL for WAGE_BILL and occupational_category=TOTAL/activity_sector=TOTAL_GENERAL for JOB/HOUR, the same filter LAB-A's original LAB-EVD-0002 used (cross-checked: JOB/HOUR YoY figures reproduce LAB-A's reported 36.75pp 2021-Q2 JOB-HOUR divergence to within rounding, 36.74pp here). METHOD: OPERATIONAL_DEFINITION filled at execution time (the hypothesis's own field deferred this to LAB-A2/LAB-A2.1 admission), without altering the hypothesis's registered METRIC/EXPECTED_OBSERVATION/FAILURE_CONDITION/POPULATION/PERIOD. LIMITATIONS: PP07H applies only to wage/salary earners (CAT_OCUP==3); self-employed, employers, and unpaid family workers are structurally excluded from this proxy (PP07H=='0' for them, confirmed by inspection, not imputed) -- this claim covers only the wage/salary-earner sub-population, not all employed persons
